newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns "senseless brutality" in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns "senseless brutality" in Burundi.

text.p: The United States on Friday condemned an increase in violence in southern Burundi, noting attacks against unarmed civilians.
"We condemn the recent acts of senseless brutality against unarmed civilians in Bururi and Makamba Provinces," State Department spokesman John Dinger said in a statement.
"Insurgent attacks against unarmed civilian populations and government reprisals against other defenceless targets are equally reprehensible," Dinger said.

He offered condolences to families of dozens of victims of an April 30 attack on a seminary in Buta, near Bururi town, and repeated a U.S. call for an end to hostilities and the start of negotiations to restore constitutional order.
In Geneva, the United Nations said on Friday dozens of people were dying daily in new outbreaks of violence in southern Burundi, where the Tutsi-dominated army is at war with majority Hutu rebels.
